In this part, we start doing meta-anlysis which for that we will use R language. If you are not familir with R language you may refer to [Link].

we will cover how we should prepare data to be imported to R studio and import data, labelling, and then analyzing codes for perfomring analysis. 

### Preparing data
For doing this, we will need to calculate the **mean change** and the **Standard Deviation (SD)** of mean change for those studies reporting only before and after measurmnets. Also, we should label our data based on defined criteria (we'll dicsuu this further below), so that we preparer them for sub-group anlyis which is very crtical in meta-anlyses. 

Let's say we have extracted the following data from study evaluating the amount of CRP:

```{r echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
install.packages("flextable")
library(flextable)

table1 <- data.frame(Pre_mean_CRP = "10.7",
           Pre_SD_CRP = "7.9",
           Post_mean_CRP = "8.7",
           Post_SD_CRP = "8.4",
           mean_change_CRP = "?",
           SD_change_CRP = "?")

flextable(table1)
```

Noe we should calcuate the mean change and SD. For doing that we can use the following formula: 

Mean Change = Post Mean - Pre Mean 

\( \text{SD}_{\text{change}} = \sqrt{(\text{Pre}_\text{SD}^2 + \text{Post}_\text{SD}^2) - 2 \times r \times \text{Pre}_\text{SD} \times \text{Post}_\text{SD}} \)

For this formual, **r** is being calculated using following formula in which Pre_SD and Post_SD should be taken from a known study in which authors themselve reported SD Change. 

\( r = \frac{\text{Pre}_\text{SD}^2 + \text{Post}_\text{SD}^2 - \text{SD}_\text{change}^2}{2 \times \text{Pre}_\text{SD} \times \text{Post}_\text{SD}} \)


For this example, we assume **r** as 0.98. Considering these formula, we can now calculate mean_change_CRP and SD_change_CRP:

```{r echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
library(flextable)

table2 <- data.frame(Pre_mean_CRP = "10.7",
           Pre_SD_CRP = "7.9",
           Post_mean_CRP = "8.7",
           Post_SD_CRP = "8.4",
           mean_change_CRP = "-2",
           SD_change_CRP = "1.70")

flextable(table2)
```


To perform subgroup analysis, we must define codes for the variables based on which we want to conduct this analysis. Common variables for subgroup analysis are:

- **Gender**
- **Dosage**
- **Duration of intervention**
- **Health status of individuals**
- **Adjustment for baseline values**
- **Study design**
- **Adherence to the intervention**

For each variable that we want to assign codes to, we create a column in Excel in front of it and place the codes there. For example, for gender we can label as follows: Both genders: Code 1, Male: Code 2, Female: Code 3. This will help us when we get into sub-group analyis, meaning we wanna the see the ffects based on this criteria, here based on geneder, and understand how gender can affect the final outcomes. 

##Analyses##

The first analysis that we get familir with is main meta-analysis which we can perfomr that in R using `metacont` or `metagen` from `meta` package. We would highly recommd to run `help(meta)` as it provides you with compehensive information on how you can run your analyses and which codes you should use.

Here we will use a sample dataset to show how we will perform our analysis.

```{r echo = FALSE, results = 'asis'}
# ── 0. Packages ───────────────────────────────────────────────
install.packages("meta")
library(readr)      # read the CSV you uploaded
library(meta)       # meta-analysis functions

# ── 1.  Read the data ─────────────────────────────────────────
sample_data <- read_csv("/Users/amirgolzan/Desktop/Sample data.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

# ── 2.  Main meta-analysis
main_analyis <- metacont(
  ## Variables for Experimental Group  (n_int, mean_change_CRP_int, SD_change_CRP_int)
  n.e      = n_int,                 ## ⇨ “Number of participants for Exp. Group: n”
  mean.e   = mean_change_CRP_int,   ## ⇨ “mean”
  sd.e     = SD_change_CRP_int,     ## ⇨ “sd”

  ## Vars for Control Group  (n_con, mean_change_CRP_con, SD_change_CRP_con)
  n.c      = n_con,                 ## ⇨ “Number of participants for Control Group: n”
  mean.c   = mean_change_CRP_con,   ## ⇨ “mean”
  sd.c     = SD_change_CRP_con,     ## ⇨ “sd”

  ## Labels  (Name = authr name)
  studlab  = `author name`,             ## ⇨ “Labels for Data  ▸ Name”
  data     = sample_data,

  ## Statistic  (noStandard → Weighted Mean Difference)
  sm       = "MD",                  ## ⇨ ‘Statistic: noStandard’

  ## Pooling model  (Fixed, Inverse-Variance)
  comb.fixed  = TRUE,               ## ⇨ ‘Pooling Model: Fixed, I-V’
  comb.random = FALSE,              ## (leave random OFF exactly as in dialog)
)

# ── 3.  Review numeric results (optional) ─────────────────────
summary(main_analyis)     # pooled WMD, I², τ², Q-test

# ── 4.  Forest plot  ↔  STATA 'Graph Opts' tab settings ──────
forest(main_analyis,
       comb.random  = FALSE,        ## show only the fixed-effect diamond
       sortvar      = year,         ## ⇨ ‘Sort Data ▸ By year’
       rightlabs    = c("WMD", "95% CI", "Weight"),
       xlab         = "Weighted Mean Difference (Δ CRP, mg/L)",
       fs.study = 9,      # study labels
       fs.axis  = 9,      # tick labels
       fs.lab   = 9)      # headings (ID, Weight, etc.)

forest(main_analyis,
       # ── layout options ────────────────────────────────────
       leftcols   = c("studlab"),                # only the author column

       rightcols  = c("effect", "ci", "w.fixed"),# WMD, 95 % CI, weight
       rightlabs  = c("WMD",   "95% CI", "Weight"),

       # ── cosmetic tweaks (optional) ────────────────────────
       sortvar    = year,        # same chronological order as before
       xlab       = "Weighted Mean Difference (Δ CRP, mg/L)",
       fs.study   = 8,           # shrink fonts if you need more rows
       fs.axis    = 8)

```
